model_annotation: This 3D line plot illustrates the relationship between accuracy (ACC, in percentage) and co-occurrence number, with different methods compared across the x-axis. The x-axis, labeled "Co-occurrence Number," uses a logarithmic scale ranging from 10¹ to 10³, with tick marks at 10¹, 10², and 10³. The y-axis, labeled "ACC (%)", is linear and ranges from 0 to 65, with tick marks every 5 units. The plot contains six distinct lines, each representing a different method: Base (black with circular markers), FT (blue with triangular markers), IKE (red with star markers), MEND (brown with diamond markers), MEMIT (purple with pentagonal markers), and ROME (green with square markers). All lines are solid and show a general downward trend as co-occurrence number increases. The ROME method (green) consistently achieves the highest accuracy, starting at approximately 46% at 10¹ and decreasing to about 37% at 10³. The Base method (black) shows the lowest accuracy, starting near 0% at 10¹ and dropping to approximately -5% at 10³. The FT method (blue) begins at around 20% and declines to about 10% at 10³. The IKE method (red) starts at about 38% and falls to roughly 20% at 10³. The MEND method (brown) starts at approximately 40%, dips slightly, and ends at around 30% at 10³. The MEMIT method (purple) begins at about 38%, rises slightly to around 39% at 10², then decreases to approximately 28% at 10³.
